builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Bit-Sparsity Aware Acceleration with Compact CSD Code on Generic Matrix Multiplication
summary: The method replaces conventional bit-parallel matrix-multiplication datapaths with a custom ASIC using compact canonical-signed-digit (CCSD) on-chip sparsification and segmented dot products for FP and QINT operands. It costs custom silicon design and fabrication at the RTL/process-node level, which a single 24 GB GPU or API-based workflow cannot use, emulate meaningfully, or procure. The gains may fail to transfer to commodity GPUs, and the claimed speedups are relative to a research accelerator (Bitlet), not to cuBLAS-class libraries readers actually run.
rationale: The contribution is a hardware architecture requiring custom silicon, so a practitioner limited to one GPU or third-party APIs can only track it for future hardware, not adopt or test it.

claims.statement: The method replaces conventional bit-parallel matrix-multiplication datapaths with a custom ASIC using compact canonical-signed-digit (CCSD) on-chip sparsification and segmented dot products for FP and QINT operands. It costs custom silicon design and fabrication at the RTL/process-node level, which a single 24 GB GPU or API-based workflow cannot use, emulate meaningfully, or procure. The gains may fail to transfer to commodity GPUs, and the claimed speedups are relative to a research accelerator (Bitlet), not to cuBLAS-class libraries readers actually run.
Compared to Bitlet, Bit-Cigma achieves 3.2x performance, 6.1x area efficiency, and 15.3x energy efficiency on FP32 with zero computing error (65 nm, 1 GHz ASIC).
